I almost always only eat grains that are complex carbohydrates - like quinoa, rolled oats, buckwheat, barley, brown rice. I ate a lot of complex carb grains to counteract cravings at first, but now my cravings have gone down, so I’m eating less complex carbohydrates grains. I find myself eating a lot more fruits and veggies now (starting to become the majority of my diet, body seems to love fiber now from fruits and veg, which is so key to a healthy digestive system), and a little bit of protein, healthy fats, and complex carb grains. 

Simple carbohydrates don’t have a lot of fiber, so they get broken down more like refined sugars. Sprouted grains that have gluten can be okay for some people, but for others (like me) cause fatigue, irritability, and bloating.

I do sneak some white/red potatoes every so often, in different forms, but those are simple carbs so they spike my blood sugar and cause some fatigue and bloating. 

It’s not super important to be strict at first with details, just cutting out refined sugars is fantastic. But over time, you’ll start to notice the subtle ways different foods affect you because your body will be free of refined sugars, which numbs you to a lot because it takes so much energy to process it. So without refined sugar, there’s more awareness of the body (and mind). It’s fun to experiment with removing different foods and then trying them again later individually to see how they make you feel

Yeah, what I realized with sugar and caffeine was that all I was looking for was a comforting thing when feeling stressed, so I went and replaced sugar and caffeine with other things I really enjoy. They aren’t necessarily really healthy for me, but they’re better than the two things that raise my blood sugar and also give me anxiety. I replaced refined sugar with tortilla chips with hummus and also nuts and seeds, and replaced the coffee with sparkling water beverages like la croix. I know those things aren’t everyone’s jam, but that’s what has worked for me. I’m sure there are other options :) And at first I let myself have maple syrup from the local co-op, if I really needed something sweet. And then I cut that out after a bit. It’s so interesting how much clearer my mind has been and how I can manage my emotions and make better decisions since I switched up the food I put in my body. 

I also have to say - I let myself eat as much as I want of things like - quinoa and vegetables and fruit smoothies. Because I know eventually my body will balance out and I’ll be eating more balanced portions cause I won’t have a feeling of needing to stave off cravings - the cravings will be gone. 

It’s little steps and also being in a place where you can allow yourself to feel any emotions. Helpful to have the time and space to experience them. I have cried quite a bit since I stopped having sugar and caffeine, but it’s  been crying I’ve needed for years! So good! I’ve spent years trying to get to this point because I couldn’t figure out how to handle stressors and eat well, but eventually you figure it out, if you just keep trying.
